heroLead: Long Creek is an unincorporated area within Williams County, sitting inside acreage that has seen substantial Bakken activity over the past decade and a half.
intro: Like other unincorporated communities scattered through Williams County, Long Creek doesn't have its own city government or a distinct downtown, but the mineral acreage in the surrounding sections has been very much part of the county's core Bakken development. Families holding an interest tied to the Long Creek area typically inherited it from farm or ranch land settled in the early 1900s, and given the level of activity in this part of the county, it's worth checking current status rather than assuming.

sections.heading: Long Creek's Position in Williams County's Core
paragraphs: This part of Williams County has seen significant horizontal drilling into both the Bakken and Three Forks formations, and spacing units here are often dense enough to include multiple wells per legal description.

sections.heading: Tracing Ownership in an Unincorporated Area
paragraphs: Because Long Creek isn't an incorporated town, records for the surrounding tracts are organized by legal description and township rather than a city address. The Williams County Recorder's office in Williston is where that deed chain lives.

sections.heading: What a Fair Look at a Long Creek Interest Involves
paragraphs: For an unincorporated-area tract like this, we start with your legal description, pull current spacing and well records against it, and only then talk through what a reasonable offer would look like, rather than quoting a number before checking the record.

faqs.question: Is Long Creek, ND part of active Bakken drilling territory?
faqs.answer: Yes, this part of Williams County has seen substantial core Bakken and Three Forks development.

faqs.question: How do I locate my Long Creek-area mineral records if there's no town address?
faqs.answer: Records for unincorporated areas are organized by legal description and township. The Williams County Recorder's office in Williston can pull the file using that description.

faqs.question: Could my Long Creek tract be part of a multi-well spacing unit?
faqs.answer: It's possible, since spacing units in this part of the county are often dense enough to hold more than one horizontal well per legal description.

faqs.question: How do I get started on a Long Creek mineral review?
faqs.answer: Send us your legal description or any existing deed, lease, or division order paperwork you have, and we'll take it from there at no cost to you.

faqs.question: Does Long Creek show up on North Dakota Industrial Commission maps?
faqs.answer: Unincorporated areas like Long Creek are represented by section, township, and range on Industrial Commission spacing and well maps rather than by community name, which is how we locate activity tied to your tract.
